assumptions: Work on \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R:|x|=1\}\) with its subspace topology and Borel sets. Use the ambient Euclidean chord \(d_{\rm ch}(x,z)=|x-z|\) and the angular cost \(c(x,z)=\arccos(xz)\).
Define \(d_{\rm len}(x,z)\) as the infimum in \([0,\infty]\) of ambient Euclidean lengths of continuous rectifiable paths \([0,1]\to S\) from \(x\) to \(z\), with empty infimum \(+\infty\).

For an extended nonnegative cost \(k\), let \(Q_k(\mu,
u)=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu,
u)}\int k\,d\gamma\), where \(\Gamma\) consists of probability measures on \(S	imes S\) with marginals \(\mu,
u\). This is the raw cost, not its square root.

mathematical_cores.question: Compute \(d_{\rm ch}(1,-1)\), \(c(1,-1)\), and \(d_{\rm len}(1,-1)\). Then compute \(Q_{c^2}(\delta_1,\delta_{-1})\) and \(Q_{d_{\rm len}^2}(\delta_1,\delta_{-1})\), proving that no other coupling changes either value. Explain why a bound on all squared angular transport costs cannot be turned into the same bound for this intrinsic squared cost by renaming the cost.

rubric.criterion: Computes chord 2 and angular cost π on the actual two-point sphere.
Uses continuity to rule out every path within S and assigns the empty path infimum +∞.

mathematical_cores.source_note: Original Samplinglib QA from the owned unit-sphere angular geometry supplement (2026-10-23), source unit 0 in the pinned sphere-feature-law-gradient lesson at commit 3212f7eb462e2d2237d0a57c6f1f425a82169cff and its antipodal scope note. Reuses the same public sphere feature-law family as sogb-032. The cited Lean and test modules are original project Apache-2.0 material; no external prose or restricted data is copied.
steps: There are exactly two points. The ambient chord is \(|1-(-1)|=2\), whereas the angular cost is \(\arccos(-1)=\pi\). The cost on the diagonal is zero. Every function on this finite Borel space, or on its square, is measurable.

A continuous path in \(S\) from \(1\) to \(-1\) would, after inclusion into \(\mathbb R\), have a zero by the intermediate value theorem. Since \(0\notin S\), no continuous path exists, in particular no rectifiable one. Thus \(d_{\rm len}(1,-1)=+\infty\), not \(2\) or \(\pi\).

Under a feasible coupling the first coordinate equals \(1\) almost surely and the second equals \(-1\) almost surely, by the two Dirac marginals. Their simultaneous event has probability one, so the feasible set is the singleton \(\{\delta_{(1,-1)}\}\). It is not empty.

Integrating an extended nonnegative function against that Dirac mass evaluates it at \((1,-1)\). Consequently \[Q_{c^2}(\delta_1,\delta_{-1})=\pi^2,\qquad Q_{d_{\rm len}^2}(\delta_1,\delta_{-1})=+\infty.\] Only the path infimum is empty. The difference in values is a change of cost, not a failed marginal condition or nonattainment of a feasible plan. This example refutes the unconditional identification even though the angular cost is finite; it does not refute a path-length identification under other dimension or connectedness hypotheses.

import Mathlib.Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.TriangleInequality
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Bounds
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

open scoped InnerProductSpace
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost

private theorem chord_le_angle
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖v‖ = 1) :
    ‖u-v‖ ≤ InnerProductGeometry.angle u v := by
  let θ := InnerProductGeometry.angle u v
  have hθ : 0 ≤ θ := InnerProductGeometry.angle_nonneg u v
  have hc : Real.cos θ = ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ := by
    simpa [θ,hu,hv] using InnerProductGeometry.cos_angle u v
  have heq : ‖u-v‖^2 = 2-2*Real.cos θ := by
    rw [norm_sub_sq_real,hu,hv,hc]
    ring
  have hh := Real.sin_sq_eq_half_sub (θ/2)
  have htwo : 2*(θ/2) = θ := by ring
  rw [htwo] at hh
  have hs := Real.sin_sq_le_sq (x := θ/2)
  change ‖u-v‖ ≤ θ
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (u-v)]

theorem unit_sphere_angular_cost_properties
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
    Continuous c ∧ Measurable c ∧
      (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧
        c (u,v) = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 ∧
        ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ c (u,v) ∧
        (c (u,v) = 0 ↔ u = v) ∧ c (u,v) = c (v,u)) ∧
      ∀ u v w : S, c (u,w) ≤ c (u,v)+c (v,w) := by
  dsimp only
  letI : SecondCountableTopology E := inferInstance
  have heq (u v : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}) :
      Real.arccos ⟪u.1,v.1⟫_ℝ = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 := by
    simp [InnerProductGeometry.angle,u.property,v.property]
  have hc : Continuous (fun z : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1} × {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1} =>
      Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ) := by fun_prop
  refine ⟨hc,hc.measurable,?_,?_⟩
  · intro u v
    have hchord : ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ Real.arccos ⟪u.1,v.1⟫_ℝ := by
      rw [heq]
      exact chord_le_angle u.1 v.1 u.property v.property
    refine ⟨Real.arccos_nonneg _,Real.arccos_le_pi _,heq u v,hchord,?_,?_⟩
    · constructor
      · intro hz
        apply Subtype.ext
        apply sub_eq_zero.mp
        apply norm_eq_zero.mp
        exact le_antisymm (by simpa only [hz] using hchord) (norm_nonneg _)
      · rintro rfl
        rw [heq]
        apply InnerProductGeometry.angle_self
        intro hz
        have hh := u.property
        rw [hz,norm_zero] at hh
        norm_num at hh
    · rw [heq,heq,InnerProductGeometry.angle_comm]
  · intro u v w
    rw [heq,heq,heq]
    exact InnerProductGeometry.angle_le_angle_add_angle u.1 v.1 w.1

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost
mathematical_cores.title: When finite angular cost is not intrinsic path distance

assumptions: Every space is \(\{0,1\}\) with all subsets measurable. The first call returns a history bit \(X\), with ideal law \({\rm Ber}(p)\) and implemented law \({\rm Ber}(q)\), for \(0\le p,q\le1\).

The ideal second call returns \(Y=0\) at either input; the implemented second call returns \(Y=X\). These rules are specified at both histories, even if one history has zero probability. The final observation is \(Y\) only.

Define hybrids \(H_0,H_1,H_2\) using respectively zero, one and two ideal calls at the beginning, with remaining calls implemented. Write \(\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\), with no extra factor in this event-supremum convention.

mathematical_cores.question: Compute the three output laws and their two adjacent total-variation gaps. Obtain the endpoint bound from the telescope and characterize when it is tight. A proposed calculation replaces the second adjacent gap by the mean of the local second-call TV under the implemented first history. Test that proposed inequality on the fixed pair \((H_1,H_2)\) at \(p=3/4,q=1/4\), and explain what went wrong. Do not claim it necessarily breaks the endpoint bound in this example.

rubric.criterion: Computes Ber(q), Ber(p), and δ₀ for the specified ideal-prefix order.
Derives the binary TV formula and both exact gaps, using the common history Ber(p) and the two local second-call discrepancies.
Uses the adjacent sum to bound the endpoint and gives the correct if-and-only-if condition q≥p for tightness.
Shows that averaging over Ber(q) fails for the fixed second adjacent pair at the specified values, without claiming that the erroneous total is a counterexample to the endpoint bound here.

The two-bit example is not attributed to that paper. It remains in the same public family as sogb-007, sogb-017 and sogb-024. Only original Apache-2.0 project material and original mathematics are distributed; no paper prose or restricted material is copied.
steps: Every stated transition is a Markov kernel; finite event probabilities and the discrepancy budget are measurable and integrable. The final output laws of \(H_0,H_1,H_2\) are respectively \({\rm Ber}(q),{\rm Ber}(p),\delta_0\): the first two use \(Y=X\), while the third uses \(Y=0\).

On the binary space the only informative events are the two singletons, whose signed probability differences are opposites. Thus the adjacent TV gaps are \(|q-p|\) and \(p\). For the first replacement the common suffix is \(Y=X\); for the second, both adjacent hybrids already use the ideal first law.

The second-call local TV is \(0\) at \(X=0\) and \(1\) at \(X=1\), so its mean under the common history \({\rm Ber}(p)\) is \(p\), exactly the second adjacent gap. Its mean under the implemented first history is \(q\), which is not the common history for \((H_1,H_2)\). At \(p=3/4,q=1/4\), the proposed bound reads \(3/4\le1/4\), so the adjacent inequality fails.

The actual endpoint TV is \(q\), and the adjacent telescope gives \(q\le |q-p|+p\). Equality holds exactly for \(q\ge p\): if \(q<p\) the sum is \(2p-q>q\). In this example the incorrectly substituted endpoint expression \(|q-p|+q\) still dominates \(q\); that numerical fact cannot repair the false claim about the second adjacent pair. A different hybrid order would require recomputing the compared laws and their common history.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelTotalVariation

/-!
# Mean conditional-kernel errors and finite hybrid telescopes

This module isolates the reusable probability-kernel core of Chen--Chewi--Lu--
Zhang, arXiv:2609.38710v1, Lemma 6.3.  If two conditional Markov kernels differ
eventwise by an integrable history-dependent bound, their output laws differ by
at most the mean of that bound.  A common downstream Markov kernel preserves
the same estimate, so later adaptive computation is absorbed by data
processing.  A finite real-valued telescope then adds the adjacent hybrid
errors.

The declarations do not construct the paper's dummy-filled history kernels,
identify its `δ_t` with a measurable total-variation function, or compare the
capped ideal algorithm with its uncapped version.  Those adapters remain
separate source obligations.
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Finset
open scoped ProbabilityTheory BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelHybridTelescope

/-- An integrable pointwise event bound between two Markov kernels controls the
corresponding event discrepancy after averaging over the input law.  This is
the mean-replacement step in the adaptive hybrid argument. -/
theorem abs_real_comp_sub_le_integral_eventBound
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (K L : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel K] [IsMarkovKernel L]
    (ε : A → ℝ) (hε : Integrable ε μ)
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s →
      |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x) :
    ∀ t, MeasurableSet t →
      |(K ∘ₘ μ).real t - (L ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤ ∫ x, ε x ∂μ := by
  intro t ht
  have hint (M : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel M] :
      Integrable (fun x => (M x).real t) μ := by
    apply (integrable_const (1 : ℝ)).mono'
      (M.measurable_coe ht).ennreal_toReal.aestronglyMeasurable
    exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg ENNReal.toReal_nonneg]
      exact (measureReal_le_one : (M x).real t ≤ 1)
  have happly (M : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel M] :
      (M ∘ₘ μ).real t = ∫ x, (M x).real t ∂μ := by
    change (Measure.bind μ M t).toReal = ∫ x, (M x t).toReal ∂μ
    rw [Measure.bind_apply ht M.aemeasurable]
    exact (integral_toReal (M.measurable_coe ht).aemeasurable
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => measure_lt_top (M x) t)).symm
  rw [happly K, happly L, ← integral_sub (hint K) (hint L)]
  exact abs_integral_le_integral_abs.trans <|
    integral_mono_ae ((hint K).sub (hint L)).abs hε <|
      hbound.mono fun x hx => hx t ht

/-- The same mean replacement bound survives a common downstream Markov
kernel.  In an adjacent adaptive hybrid, the downstream kernel represents all
later calls after the one conditional rule being replaced. -/
theorem abs_real_comp_commonSuffix_sub_le_integral_eventBound
    {A B C : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B] [MeasurableSpace C]
    (μ : Measure A) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (K L : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel K] [IsMarkovKernel L]
    (S : Kernel B C) [IsMarkovKernel S]
    (ε : A → ℝ) (hε : Integrable ε μ)
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s →
      |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x) :
    ∀ t, MeasurableSet t →
      |((S ∘ₖ K) ∘ₘ μ).real t - ((S ∘ₖ L) ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤
        ∫ x, ε x ∂μ := by
  have hKL := abs_real_comp_sub_le_integral_eventBound μ K L ε hε hbound
  have hS := KernelTotalVariation.abs_real_comp_sub_le
    (K ∘ₘ μ) (L ∘ₘ μ) S hKL
  simpa only [← Measure.comp_assoc] using hS

/-- Finite adjacent-hybrid errors telescope.  Applying this to the output laws
of hybrids `0, ..., n` turns the one-slot bounds into their accumulated error.
The result is deliberately stated for real sequences so it does not invent a
second total-variation definition. -/
theorem abs_sub_zero_le_sum_range_of_adjacent
    (a δ : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hstep : ∀ i < n, |a (i + 1) - a i| ≤ δ i) :
    |a n - a 0| ≤ ∑ i ∈ range n, δ i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      calc
        |a (n + 1) - a 0| ≤ |a (n + 1) - a n| + |a n - a 0| := by
          exact abs_sub_le _ _ _
        _ ≤ δ n + ∑ i ∈ range n, δ i :=
          add_le_add (hstep n (Nat.lt_succ_self n))
            (ih fun i hi => hstep i (hi.trans (Nat.lt_succ_self n)))
        _ = ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), δ i := by
          rw [sum_range_succ, add_comm]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelHybridTelescope
